title: de of het — en het meervoud
summary: Article gender (de vs het), the -en and -s plural rules, and why de/het matters later

blocks.title: Two words for 'the'
blocks.body: English has one 'the'. Dutch has two: **de** and **het**. Every noun is one or the other, and you mostly have to **learn it with the word** — there's no reliable rule for which. The good news: about two-thirds of nouns are *de*, and there are a few patterns you can lean on.
blocks.callout: Always learn a new noun **with its article**: not *huis* but *het huis*.

pairs.note: Anything ending in *-je* is always *het*: *het kopje* (little cup), *het meisje* (girl). No exceptions.
Even a *het* word turns to *de* in the plural: *het boek* → *de boeken*. Plurals are always *de*.

blocks.title: Learn each noun with its article

blocks.explain: *meisje* ends in *-je*, a diminutive — and every *-je* word is *het*. So *het meisje*, even though a girl is clearly a person.

blocks.title: Making plurals: -en and -s
blocks.body: Two endings cover almost everything. **-en** is the default (and most common). **-s** is used after the endings *-el, -em, -en, -er, -je* and after most vowels. Watch the spelling: a short vowel doubles its consonant (*man → mannen*), and a long vowel drops a letter (*maan → manen*).
blocks.callout: After a long single vowel (a, o, u, i) the -s takes an apostrophe: *foto's*, *auto's*, *menu's*.

blocks.prompt: Give the plural of *het boek* (the book).
blocks.hint: Default ending. No spelling change needed here.
blocks.explain: *de boeken*. Default *-en*, and remember the plural article is always *de*, never *het*.

blocks.prompt: What's the plural of *de foto* (the photo)?
blocks.explain: A long vowel at the end takes *-s* with an apostrophe: *foto's*. Same for *auto's*.

blocks.prompt: Listen and type what you hear.
blocks.explain: *twee mannen en een vrouw* — two men and a woman. *man* doubles its n in the plural.

blocks.title: Why de/het will haunt you (in a good way)
blocks.body: Right now de/het only changes 'the'. But this label sticks to the noun and controls things later: which adjective ending you use (*een groot huis* but *het grote huis*), which pointing word (*dit* vs *deze*), and which relative pronoun (*die* vs *dat*). Learning the article now is an investment — it pays off every week from here.
blocks.callout: Every noun you meet, file it as *de* or *het* on day one. Future-you says dankjewel.

blocks.prompt: Pick four objects around you. Write each with its article (guess de/het, then check), and put one into its plural.
